_note: SHRINK-ONLY RATCHET (#4956). Every coordinate here is a liveness-ledger entry that sits on a CONTAINER property and carries ONE blanket verdict for the whole subtree beneath it. Its child keys are classified NOWHERE — not in this ledger, not in another file, nowhere. That sentence is the reason this file exists: `dashboard.json` used to assert in prose that its widget keys were 'classified in the DashboardWidgetSchema subtree', no such subtree had ever existed, and the gate had no way to disagree — so `widgets[].responsive` rode straight through the #3896 inert-key sweep that removed its own sibling `widgets[].performance` and its literal namesake `view.responsive` (#4956; retired four days late in #4876 / PR #4995).
_note2: Being listed here is NOT a verdict and NOT an exemption from ADR-0049 — it is a recorded, countable gap. The gate prints how many child keys ride on inheritance on every run, and `check:liveness --undrilled` prints the worklist. A row leaves this file by being DRILLED (add `children` with a status + evidence per key, the way `view.list` / `view.form` are drilled), never by being deleted for convenience; a row whose entry has since been drilled FAILS the gate, so the debt cannot be overstated either. Adding a row is legitimate only when you have no per-key evidence to record — and it is deliberately a visible edit to a file named for the debt, because the alternative it replaced (a reassuring sentence in a `note`) cost nothing to write and could not be checked.
_excluded: ADR-0010 framework overlay fields (`protection`, `_lock*`, `_provenance` — auto-classified live, they never consult the ledger) and container properties with NO ledger row at all (already reported UNCLASSIFIED by the forward pass).
